Let the side length of each large square be \(2\). Then each square has area \(4\).

### Square I
The vertical midpoint segment intersects the diagonal at the center. The shaded triangle has perpendicular legs of length \(1\), so
\[
A_I=\frac12(1)(1)=\frac12.
\]

### Square II
The two midpoint segments divide the square into four \(1\times1\) squares. The shaded square therefore has area
\[
A_{II}=1.
\]

### Square III
The midpoint diamond has diagonals of length \(2\), so its area is
\[
\frac12(2)(2)=2.
\]
The two diagonals of the large square divide this diamond into four congruent regions. Thus the shaded region has area
\[
A_{III}=\frac{2}{4}=\frac12.
\]

Therefore,
\[
A_I=A_{III}=\frac12,\qquad A_{II}=1,
\]
so only squares \(I\) and \(III\) have equal shaded areas.

\[
\boxed{\text{C: Only the shaded areas of }I\text{ and }III\text{ are equal.}}
\]
